analysis.title: Into the Midterms
key_insights: GS notes large-cap Tech suffered outsized drawdowns after a generally underwhelming earnings slate, and EPS misses have been severely punished, especially in mega cap and AI names. It says it is hard to gauge how much is priced in.

GS names a Democratic sweep as the clear risk into the midterms. The House is less debated, and the Senate is described as a closer race. Opinions vary on whether a sweep is an equities higher or lower scenario.

Affordability is a common theme across Democratic and Republican agendas. GS says the more actionable question is which policy areas become easier to negotiate, get more regulatory attention, or gain leverage in future spending debates.
Five themes are in focus: ACA subsidies and health insurance affordability, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending, and corporate tax.
In a Democratic sweep, GS's favorite long is the ACA Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA), made up of hospitals and similar businesses, and it says the basket offers an attractive entry level.

GS expects AI datacenters and hardware (GSTMTDAT) could pull back in a Democratic sweep. It expects the Power theme (GSENEPOW) to outperform if increasing power supply is portrayed as the answer to electricity inflation.

Power inflation: the debate is moving from whether datacenters should be built to who pays for the added power generation and transmission. GS calls this one of the more underappreciated election-sensitive themes. Utilities and grid operators could benefit from regulatory clarity, while economics for some datacenter projects become less attractive.

Drug pricing: both parties favor expanding Medicare price negotiation, MFN benchmark pricing, redefining the exclusivity clock, and stricter Medicaid and PBM obligations. GS recommends a short on the Drug-Makers basket (GSHLCBPH). MRK and AMGN have identified drugs that could face price setting from 2028.

Government spending: Congress has run on continuing resolutions, and the current CR expires in December. GS sees scope for debate on broader spending increases, which could support non-defense spending beneficiaries. It is long the ex-Defense Government-Spending basket (GSXUGOVT) and short Defense Spending Beneficiaries (GSXUDFNS).

Corporate tax: the 21% rate and several TCJA business provisions (including 100% bonus depreciation) are permanent after the 2025 OBBBA. A presidential veto makes midterm tax changes unlikely. GS says 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated, and the risk is to valuations beyond 2029.

Tariffs: GS says investors should be cautious about assuming tariff relief. Congressional Democrats have limited ability to reverse tariffs, and the administration continues to impose them under alternative authorities after the Supreme Court invalidated the IEEPA tariffs. GS sees more risk of tariffs moving higher than lower between now and early 2027, and suggests shorting Tariff-Sensitive Equities.

Other election-sensitive calls: short Big Tech on antitrust risk, short Investment Banks and crypto-exposed equities on financial regulation risk, and long Homebuilders on potential housing tax credits and first-time buyer incentives.
GS is hosting three midterm webinars on Nov 4 (SGT) and one on Nov 2 with Eric Sheridan on US Internet after 3Q earnings.

market_movers.rationale: MRK has identified drugs that could face Medicare price setting from 2028, leading to a projected decline in US sales.
AMGN has identified drugs that could face Medicare price setting from 2028, leading to a projected decline in US sales.

sector_views.rationale: A Democratic sweep would likely restore enhanced ACA subsidies and bring patient volumes back, reducing bad debt and uncompensated care.
Both parties favor drug price controls, and Democrats would likely expand the number of drugs negotiated each year.
Regulatory clarity on who pays for datacenter power could benefit utilities and grid operators.
Ratepayer protection policies could shift power infrastructure costs onto datacenters and make some projects less attractive.
Democrats push for parity between defense and domestic spending, and GS is short the Defense Spending Beneficiaries basket.
Democratic leaders could push for stricter antitrust oversight.
A less favorable regulatory backdrop and a rebuilt CFPB could dampen capital markets activity.
Democrats could differentiate with expanded housing tax credits and first-time homebuyer incentives.
GS sees more risk of tariffs rising than falling by early 2027.

earnings_insights: GS describes the 3Q earnings slate for large-cap Tech as generally underwhelming, with EPS misses severely punished, especially in mega cap and AI names. The note gives no company-level figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A Democratic House or Senate gains agenda and oversight control, but a presidential veto makes a rate change unlikely. A higher rate would cut after-tax income for full-rate payers, with the risk to valuations beyond 2029.

crypto_views: GS suggests shorting cryptocurrency-exposed equities because a Democratic push on financial regulation could create a less favorable regulatory backdrop.

trade_ideas.description: Long ACA-Exposed Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA) in a Democratic sweep scenario
trade_ideas.rationale: Restoring enhanced ACA subsidies would return patient volumes to providers and reduce bad debt and uncompensated care.
Both parties back drug price negotiation, MFN pricing and stricter PBM obligations.

trade_ideas.description: Long Renewables (GSXURNEW), Grid Infrastructure (GSXUGRID) and Power Up America (GSENEPOW), including the AI Power vs AI Hardware ex-Power pair (GSPUAIPO)
trade_ideas.rationale: The debate is shifting to who pays for datacenter power, which could give utilities and grid operators regulatory clarity.

trade_ideas.description: Buy protection on Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) and Datacenter Equipment (GSTMTDAT)
trade_ideas.rationale: Ratepayer protection policies could shift power costs onto datacenters and make some projects less attractive.

trade_ideas.description: Long Government-Spending Exposed ex-Defense and Drug-Makers basket (GSXUGOVT), short Defense Spending Beneficiaries basket (GSXUDFNS)
trade_ideas.rationale: Debate over broader spending increases could pick up before the December CR expiry and support non-defense spending beneficiaries.

trade_ideas.description: Short Big Tech on antitrust risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Democratic leaders have criticized current antitrust controls and may push for stricter oversight of Big Tech.

trade_ideas.description: Short Investment Banks and Cryptocurrency-exposed equities
trade_ideas.rationale: A rebuilt CFPB and Wall Street oversight could create a less favorable regulatory backdrop.
GS sees more risk of tariffs moving higher than lower between now and early 2027.
Democrats could expand housing tax credits and first-time homebuyer incentives.
trade_ideas.risk: Significant fiscal measures would still require presidential approval.

trade_ideas.description: Corporate Tax basket (GSPUTAXP) flagged as an early theme to trade
trade_ideas.rationale: A Democratic House or Senate would gain agenda and oversight control, and moving above the 21% rate would reduce after-tax income for full-rate payers.
trade_ideas.risk: Presidential veto makes a change in tax law unlikely.

risk_factors: A Democratic sweep is the clear risk into the midterms, and opinions vary on whether it is bullish or bearish for equities.
Large-cap Tech earnings misses are being severely punished, and it is hard to tell how much is priced in.
Datacenter ratepayer protection policy could shift power infrastructure costs onto datacenters.
Continuing resolution expires in December, with spending debate likely.
Tariffs could move higher between now and early 2027.
A higher corporate tax rate would put valuations beyond 2029 at risk.
vol_and_positioning: GS suggests buying protection on Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) and Datacenter Equipment (GSTMTDAT) as a hedge for a Democratic sweep and ratepayer protection policies.
geopolitical: US-Iran: GS says opinions vary on what a Democratic sweep would mean for geopolitics, citing US-Iran.

tension_points.bull_case: Opinions vary, and some see a Democratic sweep as an equities higher scenario. GS's long ideas in a sweep are ACA beneficiaries, power and grid names, non-defense government spending and homebuilders.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic sweep could mean a pullback in AI datacenters and hardware, tougher antitrust and financial regulation, and tariff risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Midterm results other than a Democratic sweep, with GS saying the Senate is a closer race than the House.

tension_points.bull_case: Regulatory clarity on cost-bearing benefits utilities and grid operators, and the Power theme outperforms if increasing power supply is the solution to electricity inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Ratepayer protection shifts power infrastructure costs onto datacenters, making some projects less attractive and weighing on hyperscalers and datacenter equipment.
